timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: I installed a firewall on my computer. I'm safe now, right?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Peter, a firewall is like a bouncer at a club. It checks who's coming in and who's going out based on rules. But it can't stop someone who's dressed as a legitimate guest.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Firewalls filter traffic based on rules - IP addresses, ports, protocols. But they can't inspect encrypted traffic without special configuration. The SolarWinds attackers used legitimate HTTPS to exfiltrate data.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: There are different types: packet filtering firewalls check headers, stateful firewalls track connection states, and next-gen firewalls can inspect application content.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So I need a next-gen one?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Not necessarily. The best firewall is useless if the rules are wrong. I've seen companies with default 'allow all' rules. Configuration matters more than the product.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Host-based firewalls protect individual machines. Network firewalls protect the perimeter. You need both. Defense in depth.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Cloud firewalls, or WAFs, protect web applications. They filter HTTP traffic and can block SQL injection, XSS, and other application-layer attacks. Every production web app needs one.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Interview tip: explain the difference between stateful and stateless firewalls, and when you'd use each. Also know how firewalls can be bypassed.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So firewalls are important but not the whole picture?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. They're one layer. You also need IDS/IPS, endpoint protection, encryption, and security awareness. No single tool makes you secure.
